clue.text: Pontificate about source of rapid growth

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth pompously, as a pontificator does

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of rapid

explanation.surface: A pompous speaker holds forth about something that shoots up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pontificate' reads as the definition at the head of the clue, but the definition is the last word, 'growth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a fresh shoot, new plant growth emerging from a seed or stem.

clue.text: Upset South American alliance about capital of Colombia — or elsewhere?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the single letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: standard abbreviation for South American
a union is an alliance

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the initial letter of Colombia

explanation.surface: A political bloc in South America falls apart over the Colombian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is partly wordplay: 'capital of Colombia' gives C, while the whole phrase, with its 'or elsewhere?', points to a capital in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay, so it is a South American capital, just not Colombia's.

clue.text: Bird from cold region flying for nicer tract?

indicators.note: flying suggests things scattered through the air, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A bird leaves its frozen home and migrates in search of pleasanter land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: this seabird famously makes the longest migration of any bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic tern is a seabird that breeds in polar northern regions, hence a bird from a cold place.

clue.text: Bird appearing in fight after fight

indicators.note: after places the second word's letters following the first word's letters

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A bird gets into one scrap after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The two identical words give different synonyms: SPAR then ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, common in towns and gardens.

clue.text: Youngster offering no initial assistance

indicators.note: no initial says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a whelp is a young dog, or loosely a youngster

explanation.surface: A young person gives no help at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and assistance are straightforward synonyms, meaning aid or support given to someone.

clue.text: Attack when ahead of fleet

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first word's letters before those of the next

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sail can mean a number of ships, a fleet

explanation.surface: A naval commander attacks at the moment his ships draw ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, either physically or with criticism.

clue.text: Agreement's peculiar language about kitchen appliance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the language word goes around the appliance

parts.note: cant is the jargon or slang peculiar to a group
an oven is a kitchen appliance

explanation.surface: A contract uses odd jargon on the subject of a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means 'belonging to a particular group', the sense in which cant is a group's own language.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding promise or contract between parties, as in a deed.

clue.text: Rhetorical trick is perhaps too complicated

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A speechmaking device may be overly elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the punctuation mark: in rhetoric the word also names a speaker's sudden address to someone absent.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, an apostrophe is a figure of speech turning aside to address an absent person or abstraction.

clue.text: Social climber's insulting comment about name

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the insult wraps the single letter

parts.note: SOB, short for 'son of a bitch', is an insult
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An upwardly mobile person makes a rude remark about someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: S(N)OB. SOB is the initialism for a crude insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob admires those of higher status and seeks to rise among them, a typical social climber.

clue.text: Ice-cream's central temperature brought about liquefaction at last

indicators.note: brought about means put round, so the joined pieces enclose the single letter

parts.note: the core is the central part
T is the abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of liquefaction

explanation.surface: An ice cream's middle warmed up and it melted in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: COR(N)E T: N slips into CORE plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a cornet is an ice-cream cone, or a cone filled with ice cream.

clue.text: Grass seen around boggy stuff on a regular basis

definitions.note: adverbial phrase; the answer is an adjective, as in 'repeated visits'

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the grass word goes about the bog material

parts.note: a reed is a tall water grass
peat is the decomposed matter found in bogs

explanation.surface: Reeds grow around the edges of a peat bog year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeated happens again and again, so it recurs frequently and routinely.

clue.text: Case that is recalled, involving you in Calais

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the French word goes inside
recalled means called back, so the letters for 'that is' run backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
tu is French for you, as spoken in the French port of Calais

explanation.surface: A legal case is remembered, one that involved you on a trip to Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles, scissors or cosmetics, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Caught one really liking page showing part of road network

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a lover is someone who really likes something
a leaf is a page of a book

explanation.surface: Someone who adores a certain page has been caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloverleaf is a motorway interchange whose looping slip roads resemble a four-leafed clover.

clue.text: Ensure boat is at sea in coastal resort

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Make sure the boat is out on the water at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastbourne is a seaside town on England's south coast, in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a traditional English seaside town, popular with holidaymakers and retirees.

clue.text: Oblique impact from tip of whirling weapon

indicators.note: the tip is the very end, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of whirling
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A spinning weapon delivers a blow at an angle with its point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' looks like an anagram signal but only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a blow that strikes at an angle and slides off, as in a glancing blow.

clue.text: Fish lake getting knickers etc.

parts.note: the ling is a long cod-like sea fish
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An angler on a lake hauls in underwear instead of a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Knickers is the British word for women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, of which knickers are one example.

clue.text: Tight dress? Keep quiet, suppressing passion

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sh is the instruction to keep quiet
heat is intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: Someone in a figure-hugging dress is told to hush and keep her passion in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting dress, and the question mark nods to the other sense of a tight covering.

clue.text: Moral expert I see probing this when detained by alien

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so the first pair goes into the next word

parts.note: ET is the film alien

indicators.note: detained by means held inside, so the result sits within the alien

parts.note: taken as written
I as written, plus C, which sounds like 'see'

explanation.surface: A moral philosopher realises something is under investigation while held by an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'I see' goes into 'this' first, and that result is held by the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethicist is someone who studies or advises on ethics, the principles of right and wrong.

clue.text: European and American engaged in broadcasting now may be hard to find

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: engaged in means taken up within, so the American letters sit inside the broadcasting word

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A European and an American on live air might be tricky to track down.
explanation.definitionFit: Elusive describes something that evades capture or is difficult to locate or pin down.

clue.text: On radio, I will take point about limitations of crucial gym item

parts.note: India is the radio code word for the letter I in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the point word goes around the outer letters

parts.note: the nub is the point or crux of a matter

indicators.note: limitations are boundaries, so the outer letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of crucial

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces she will make a key point about what limits fitness equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On radio' looks like a homophone signal; it means the radio alphabet, where I is spoken as INDIA. Then N(CL)UB.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian club is a bottle-shaped wooden club swung in pairs for gymnastic exercise.

clue.text: Take a breath, having almost bisected base of tree

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: something bisected is cut in half

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of tree

explanation.surface: A lumberjack pauses for breath having nearly sawn through the bottom of a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to draw air into the lungs, which is what taking a breath means.

clue.text: Husband leading a pair of judges in pilgrimage

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first letter comes before the rest

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge, so two of them

explanation.surface: A husband heads two judges on a religious journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hajj is the annual Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, required once of those able to make it.

clue.text: Beer almost completed in a manner of speaking?

indicators.note: almost means short of complete, so the word for completed loses its last letter

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer
gone can mean finished or done with

explanation.surface: Having nearly finished a beer, someone speaks in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is British slang for a pint or glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the special vocabulary of a trade or group, a particular way of speaking; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Security components presenting significant difficulties

parts.note: key means important or significant
holes are tight spots or difficulties, as in 'in a hole'

explanation.surface: Parts of a security system turn out to be causing serious problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyholes are the openings in locks into which keys fit, so they are parts of securing doors.

clue.text: Pale lines circling one yard

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the lines enclose the numeral

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Faint markings run around one yard of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily as an adjective, as in lily-white, means pale or white like the flower.

clue.text: Straighten out relative, mostly about ancient city

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened relative goes round the city
mostly means not entirely, so the relative loses its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A relative sets the record straight on the history of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncurl is to unwind from a curled position, making something straight or flat again.

clue.text: English philosopher's focus of development during the Industrial Revolution?

definitions.meaning: John Stuart ..., the nineteenth-century English philosopher of liberty and utilitarianism

definitions.text: focus of development during the Industrial Revolution?
definitions.meaning: textile factories were at the heart of Britain's industrial growth

explanation.surface: A historian asks what one English thinker concentrated on during the industrial age.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but simply links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a leading English philosopher, and the cotton factory was central to industrialisation.

clue.text: Means of support not held back in Scottish town

parts.note: livings are incomes, ways of supporting oneself

indicators.note: held back suggests turning back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Support is withheld in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Livingston is a new town in West Lothian, between Edinburgh and Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Livingston is a town in central Scotland, developed as a new town after the Second World War.
